page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-1 is an Arm-based virtual machine configured with a high memory-to-vCPU allocation. The hardware profile comprises 1 dedicated vCPU mapped to 1 physical core on an ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz. The processor subsystem includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and an 80 MB L3 cache. It provides 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, depending entirely on remote block storage solutions for persistent data.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance delivered by the Neoverse-V2 core. In Geekbench single-core testing, the instance scores 1957.0 points, placing it in the upper quartile of tested systems. Single-threaded data throughput is similarly robust, achieving 32.1 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.05 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate processing capacity is bound by the single-core footprint, resulting in a Geekbench multi-core score of 1952.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 1061.04. Memory testing demonstrates average throughput, with a PassMark memory score of 1916.49, uncached read bandwidth of 29.49 GB/sec, and uncached write bandwidth of 11.76 GB/sec.

The c4a-highmem-1 instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for software that demands memory capacity without requiring parallel processing resources. Operating a single core limits operational overhead for workloads that do not scale across multiple threads. The primary tradeoff is the strict ceiling on concurrency and dependence on networked storage. The instance fits lightweight database systems, small in-memory caches, background ETL tasks with modest compute needs, and low-traffic web services.
